text:
Your shuttle weaves through a maze of docking arms, cargo cranes, and half-finished station modules before disappearing into the sprawling patchwork that is Reda. Guided by flashing maintenance lights, it arrives in a different hangar where crews, forklifts, and construction machinery compete for every square meter of space.

Following faded signs through reinforced corridors and welded passageways, you eventually reach the station's dockside bar. Mechanics, salvagers, and freighter crews gather around tables assembled from reclaimed bulkheads while the distant rhythm of riveters echoes through the walls.

Your shuttle is led across the fuel harvesting platform to a distant port.

A short walk through quiet industrial corridors leads to the platform's modest dockside bar. Only a handful of workers occupy the room, while autonomous machines continue operating beyond the reinforced windows. Outside, maintenance drones drift through turbulent skies as the endless roar of compressors vibrates faintly through the floor.

Taking a fast shuttle parking closeby, you pass between two towering arcologies until you land again onto a pristine landing platform on the side of the spaceport.

A network of illuminated walkways leads directly into one of Kama's entertainment districts. The dockside bar blends seamlessly into the surrounding skyline, its polished interior filled with softly glowing holograms, robotic attendants, and patrons whose conversations are often quieter than the silent exchange of data between their neural implants. It is difficult to shake the feeling that every movement within the room is being quietly observed.

Taking a parked shuttle slipping through muscled tubes you take off to the dockside bar.

After disembarking, you follow heavy industrial corridors into the bar. The walls and supporting columns are covered in distorted faces and malformed statues, imperfections left behind by gigantic construction printers that no one ever chose to correct. Many people are in here and half of them are biologically upgraded, show leathery skin, extra muscles or joints. Between conversations, the floor trembles as distant fabrication complexes begin another production cycle. No one reacts. For the people of Utroba, the unsettling architecture has long since become ordinary.

Your shuttle lands amidst rows of modular buildings, reinforced bunkers, and hastily expanded docking facilities. Cargo vehicles and construction equipment weave between workshops assembled from salvaged hull sections, while the distant sound of welding and heavy machinery seems to come from every direction.

The dockside bar is made of reclaimed armor plates as walls, mismatched furniture surrounding tables and every patron seems to have arrived straight from a repair bay or salvage operation. Conversations are loud, drinks are strong, and somewhere beyond the walls another structure is already being dismantled so its materials can be used elsewhere.

Your shuttle glides effortlessly into a perfectly synchronized stream of air traffic before touching down at an immaculate landing platform. Autonomous service drones unload cargo while silent transit systems carry passengers into the heart of the settlement beneath towering neon-lit arcologies.

The dockside bar is elegant without being extravagant. Soft lighting reflects from polished metal and glass while robotic attendants serve customers with flawless precision. Most conversations are brief, often interrupted by silent exchanges through cybernetic implants or augmented displays. Though the atmosphere is calm and welcoming, the subtle presence of surveillance systems and the constant awareness of artificial intelligences leaves the unsettling impression that nothing within here ever goes unnoticed.

Your shuttle descends toward immense structures that seem almost carved rather than constructed. Colossal buildings rise from the surrounding area in layered formations, their surfaces interrupted by distorted faces, malformed statues, and organic-looking support columns created by the settlement's enormous construction printers.

The dockside bar lies within one of these cast printed structures. Warm air carries the scent of machine oil, antiseptics, and unfamiliar biological compounds as ship crews gather beneath towering vaulted ceilings.
